editorial.headline: Wholesale Fertiliser and Agrochemicals: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale fertiliser and agrochemical trade is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent moratorium prevents PMA registration of the activity there.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is a wholesale-trade activity: fertilisers and agrochemical—agricultural chemical—products are the goods named in its scope. The definition matters because it identifies the commercial activity through both its mode of trade and its product set. A business registering here is identifying its work as wholesale trade in those products. That is the fixed centre of the activity, and the reference point for reading its available scales and investment position.

The record opens the activity to every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. In other words, the wholesale trade described here is available across all four classifications listed in the record. The essential question remains straightforward: whether the enterprise’s activity is the wholesale trade of fertilisers and agrochemical products. The scale field then confirms that each of the four named classifications is open for that activity.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is just as unambiguous. The status is open, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. A foreign investor may therefore hold the full stake in a nationally registered business carrying on this wholesale activity. That national position is grounded in the cited Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. It is an important answer, but only to the national ownership question; it does not by itself settle whether a PMA registration can proceed in a particular province.

Bali produces the decisive qualification. This activity is marked as blocked for PMA registration there because, at the Large scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registrations in those risk categories. The result is plain: nationally open at 100% does not translate into the ability to register this PMA activity in Bali today. The provincial restriction does not change the activity’s wholesale scope or its national foreign-ownership ceiling; it determines the local registration outcome in Bali, where the activity is blocked under the recorded risk classification and moratorium of May 2026.
